name: The Parade
description: The Berland Army is preparing for a large military parade. It is already decided that the soldiers participating in it will be divided into $$$k$$$ rows, and all rows will contain the same number of soldiers. Of course, not every arrangement of soldiers into $$$k$$$ rows is suitable. Heights of all soldiers in the same row should not differ by more than $$$1$$$. The height of each soldier is an integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$n$$$. For each possible height, you know the number of soldiers having this height. To conduct a parade, you have to choose the soldiers participating in it, and then arrange all of the chosen soldiers into $$$k$$$ rows so that both of the following conditions are met: each row has the same number of soldiers, no row contains a pair of soldiers such that their heights differ by $$$2$$$ or more. Calculate the maximum number of soldiers who can participate in the parade.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10000$$$) — the number of test cases. Then the test cases follow. Each test case begins with a line containing two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 30000$$$, $$$1 \le k \le 10^{12}$$$) — the number of different heights of soldiers and the number of rows of soldiers in the parade, respectively. The second (and final) line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$c_1$$$, $$$c_2$$$, ..., $$$c_n$$$ ($$$0 \le c_i \le 10^{12}$$$), where $$$c_i$$$ is the number of soldiers having height $$$i$$$ in the Berland Army. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$30000$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the maximum number of soldiers that can participate in the parade.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1250J — The Parade [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
